definitions.gloss: extra edition; special edition (of a newspaper)
definitions.explanation: A special newspaper edition published outside the regular schedule to report breaking news of major importance. Traditionally distributed free on the street.

examples.japanese: {号外|ごうがい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}た→出る：00513_deru⟧。
⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{号外|ごうがい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{配|くば}っていた→配る：03921_kubaru⟧。
examples.english: They were handing out extra editions in front of the station.

examples.japanese: ⟦{戦争|せんそう}→戦争：01450_sensou⟧⟦{終結|しゅうけつ}→終結：13851_shuuketsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ニュース→ニュース：04437_nyuusu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{号外|ごうがい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{伝|つた}えられ→伝える：01220_tsutaeru⟧、⟦{人々|ひとびと}→人々：03141_hitobito⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{歓声|かんせい}→歓声：02686_kansei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{上|あ}げた→上げる：02443_ageru⟧。
examples.english: The news of the war's end was announced in an extra edition, and people cheered.

notes:
Composed of {号|ごう} (number, issue) and ⟦{外|がい}→外〜：03948_gai⟧ (outside) — literally an issue 'outside' the regular numbering. A {号外|ごうがい} is published only for truly major events: elections, natural disasters, historic achievements, or declarations of war/peace.

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, {号外|ごうがい} are traditionally single-sheet papers distributed by hand near train stations. Even in the digital age, major newspapers still print physical {号外|ごうがい} for landmark events, and crowds gather to receive them as keepsakes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {号外|ごうがい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧ — an extra edition comes out
- {号外|ごうがい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{配|くば}る→配る：03921_kubaru⟧ — to distribute extra editions
- {号外|ごうがい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧ — to publish an extra edition
